# BR-500 Control Narrative: pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control

**Scope:** 2000 L single-use CHO bioreactor BR-500, DeltaV DCS, ISA-88 batch.
**Status:** DRAFT. Items marked **[TBD]** need values from the process owner or FDS before OQ protocol writing.

Each requirement has an ID (e.g., PH-03) so OQ test cases can trace to it. Section 6 gives a suggested OQ test matrix.

---

## 1. Instruments and Final Control Elements

| Tag | Description | Role |
|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH probes | Redundant measurement |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO probes | Redundant measurement |
| FCV-510 | CO2 sparge flow control valve, 0-2 slpm | pH acid side |
| P-520 | 1 M sodium carbonate pump | pH base side |
| WT-521 | Load cell, base bag | Cumulative base addition |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller, 80-140 rpm | DO stage 1 |
| FCV-511 | Air sparge control valve, 0-10 slpm | DO stage 2 |
| FCV-512 | O2 sparge control valve, 0-5 slpm | DO stage 3 |

## 2. Phase Applicability

- **PHA-01:** pH and DO control shall be active only in the Equilibrate, Inoculate, and Production phases. Inoculate is included because it lies between Equilibrate and Production.
- **PHA-02:** In Media Fill and Harvest, pH and DO loops shall be in Manual/out of service, and CO2, base, air and O2 outputs shall be at their safe state (valves closed, P-520 stopped). The agitator is controlled by the phase logic of those phases, not by the DO loop.
- **PHA-03:** On the transition into Equilibrate, loops shall start in Auto with the setpoints in Section 3 and 4. On the transition into Harvest, loops shall be placed out of service and outputs set to safe state.
- **PHA-04:** On batch Hold or Abort, outputs shall go to the **[TBD: hold state, e.g. last position vs. safe state]**.

## 3. pH Control

### 3.1 Measurement and Validation
- **PH-01:** The controlled pH PV shall be the average of AT-501A and AT-501B when both are healthy.
- **PH-02:** A probe is unhealthy if it has a bad signal status/out-of-range, or if it deviates from the other probe by more than **[TBD] pH units for more than [TBD] s**.
- **PH-03:** If one probe is unhealthy, control shall continue automatically on the healthy probe and a probe-fault alarm shall be raised identifying the probe.
- **PH-04:** If both probes are unhealthy, pH control shall go to the **[TBD: fail-safe state]** with CO2 and base outputs at 0, and a high-priority alarm raised.
- **PH-05:** A high probe deviation alarm (A vs. B) shall be raised at **[TBD]**, before probe exclusion where applicable.

### 3.2 Setpoint and Deadband
- **PH-06:** pH setpoint = **7.00**. Deadband = **±0.05** (control band 6.95 to 7.05).
- **PH-07:** Within the deadband, both CO2 and base outputs shall be 0.
- **PH-08:** The control algorithm (split-range PID vs. on/off with deadband) is **[TBD per FDS]**. The requirement is the behavior in PH-07, PH-09, and PH-10.

### 3.3 Acid Side (CO2)
- **PH-09:** When PV > SP + 0.05, FCV-510 shall modulate between 0 and 2 slpm to lower pH. FCV-510 output shall never exceed 2 slpm, and shall be 0 when PV is at or below the upper deadband limit.

### 3.4 Base Side (Sodium Carbonate)
- **PH-10:** When PV < SP - 0.05, P-520 shall dose 1 M sodium carbonate to raise pH. Dose rate/pulse parameters **[TBD]**.
- **PH-11:** CO2 and base shall never be actively dosed at the same time.

### 3.5 Base Total Limit (40 L)
- **PH-12:** Cumulative base added per batch shall be calculated from WT-521 weight loss, reset at batch start only (not at phase change). **[TBD: density conversion, reset rule on bag change]**
- **PH-13:** A pre-limit warning alarm shall be raised at **[TBD, e.g. 35 L]**.
- **PH-14:** At cumulative base ≥ **40 L**, P-520 shall be stopped and inhibited for the remainder of the batch, and a high-priority alarm raised. pH control shall continue on the acid side only.
- **PH-15:** If WT-521 signal is bad, P-520 shall be inhibited (fail-safe) and an alarm raised **[TBD: confirm with process owner]**.
- **PH-16:** Resuming base addition after the 40 L inhibit shall require an authorized override with audit trail **[TBD: or not permitted]**.

## 4. DO Control

### 4.1 Measurement
- **DO-01:** DO PV shall be the average of AT-502A and AT-502B when both are healthy.
- **DO-02:** Probe health, single-probe fallback and dual-failure behavior shall follow the same pattern as PH-02 to PH-05, with deviation limits **[TBD]**.

### 4.2 Setpoint
- **DO-03:** DO setpoint = **40% air saturation**. Deadband/hysteresis **[TBD]**.

### 4.3 Cascade Sequence
Demand for more oxygen shall be met in this strict order:

1. **Stage 1: Agitation.** SIC-530 shall increase from **80 rpm** up to **140 rpm**.
2. **Stage 2: Air sparge.** Only when SIC-530 is at 140 rpm, FCV-511 shall increase from 0 to **10 slpm**.
3. **Stage 3: O2 sparge.** Only when FCV-511 is at 10 slpm, FCV-512 shall increase from 0 to **5 slpm**.

- **DO-04:** SIC-530 shall remain within 80-140 rpm whenever DO control is active.
- **DO-05:** FCV-511 shall not open above its minimum **[TBD: baseline flow]** until SIC-530 is at 140 rpm. FCV-512 shall not open until FCV-511 is at 10 slpm.
- **DO-06:** When DO demand decreases, the cascade shall unwind in reverse order: O2 first, then air, then agitation.
- **DO-07:** Limits: FCV-511 ≤ 10 slpm, FCV-512 ≤ 5 slpm.
- **DO-08:** Stage handover shall include anti-windup and bumpless transfer, with hysteresis **[TBD]** to avoid chattering between stages.
- **DO-09:** Whether agitation has a lower floor below 80 rpm, and the interaction of the agitator with phase-specific minimum mixing, is **[TBD]**.
- **DO-10:** Low DO alarm at **[TBD]**, high DO alarm at **[TBD]**, with delay **[TBD]**.
- **DO-11:** Total gas flow interaction with the CO2 sparge (pH) and overlay/vent limits **[TBD]**.

## 5. Setpoint Change Recording (Production Phase)

- **SP-01:** Any change to pH SP, pH deadband, DO SP (and, **[TBD per QA]**, cascade limits and tuning) during the Production phase shall require a reason to be entered before the change is accepted.
- **SP-02:** The record shall contain: parameter tag, old value, new value, date/time, user ID, and reason. It shall be stored in the batch record/audit trail and be non-editable.
- **SP-03:** Change shall require a role with the proper privilege (**[TBD]**). A change cancelled or without a reason shall not be applied.
- **SP-04:** Changes made in other phases follow standard audit trail logging, with a reason not mandatory **[TBD: confirm with QA]**.
- **SP-05:** Recipe-driven setpoint changes shall be recorded with the recipe step as the reason.

## 6. Suggested OQ Test Matrix

| Test | Requirements | Method | Expected result |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 Phase activation | PHA-01, 02, 03 | Step the batch through all five phases | Loops active only Equilibrate to Production; outputs safe in others |
| OQ-02 pH averaging | PH-01 | Simulate A and B at different values | PV = mean |
| OQ-03 Probe fault | PH-02, 03, 05 | Fail or drift one probe | Alarm, control continues on healthy probe |
| OQ-04 Dual probe fault | PH-04 | Fail both | Defined fail-safe state, alarm |
| OQ-05 Deadband | PH-06, 07 | Hold PV at 6.95-7.05 | No CO2, no base |
| OQ-06 Acid action | PH-09 | Simulate PV above 7.05 | FCV-510 opens, ≤ 2 slpm |
| OQ-07 Base action | PH-10, 11 | Simulate PV below 6.95 | P-520 doses; no simultaneous CO2 |
| OQ-08 Base limit | PH-12 to 14 | Simulate WT-521 loss to warning level and 40 L | Warning, then P-520 stops and is inhibited; acid continues |
| OQ-09 Load cell fault | PH-15 | Fail WT-521 | P-520 inhibited, alarm |
| OQ-10 Cascade up | DO-03 to 05 | Drive DO below SP | Order: agitation, air, O2; limits respected |
| OQ-11 Cascade down | DO-06 | Restore DO above SP | Reverse order |
| OQ-12 DO probe fault | DO-01, 02 | As OQ-03/04 for AT-502 | As specified |
| OQ-13 Setpoint change | SP-01 to 03 | Change pH/DO SP in Production with and without reason; with an unauthorized user | Only valid, reasoned change accepted and recorded; others rejected |
| OQ-14 Hold/Abort | PHA-04 | Hold and abort during Production | Defined output state |

## 7. Open Items for Process Owner / QA
Items marked **[TBD]** above: probe deviation limits and delays, control algorithm and tuning, base dosing parameters, 35 L warning value, load cell fault handling and override rule, DO alarms and hysteresis, agitator floor, Hold/Abort states, and which parameters beyond setpoints fall under SP-01.
